name: ChatGPT
description: ChatGPT is OpenAI's AI assistant app, offering chat, voice, vision, and agentic "Work"/"Codex" capabilities for asking questions, researching, and creating documents.
best_for: Positioned by OpenAI as a general assistant for chatting, searching, research/analysis, document/spreadsheet/presentation creation ("Work"), and software development with local files and terminals ("Codex").
features: "Work" mode for research and document/spreadsheet/deck creation

alternatives.name: Perplexity
alternatives.description: An AI answer engine that researches the open web in real time and returns concise, cited answers.
alternatives.best_for: People who want real-time, cited answers to questions rather than a list of links.

alternatives.name: Gemini
alternatives.description: Google DeepMind's family of AI models for building and using intelligent agents across text, image, video, and audio.
alternatives.best_for: Developers, enterprises, and consumers already in the Google ecosystem needing agentic or long-context reasoning.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.notes: No cost. Unlimited text chat 'subject to abuse guardrails'; limited uploads, image generation, voice, deep research, memory/context.

tiers.name: Go
tiers.notes: Monthly billing only (OpenAI's own FAQ lists monthly plans for Go, Plus, Business; annual only for Business/Enterprise). May include ads per the plan's own footnote.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.notes: Annual option available at $16.67/user/month (effectively ~$200/year, i.e. ~2 months free vs monthly). Page states 'Limits apply' rather than a published hard usage cap.

tiers.name: Pro (entry tier)
tiers.notes: Displayed as the 'From' price on the Pro card; sits between Plus ($20) and the higher Pro tier ($200).

tiers.name: Pro (top tier)
tiers.notes: Top individual tier. Usage described as 'Unlimited subject to abuse guardrails' -- no published numeric cap.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.notes: Minimum 2 seats (per OpenAI FAQ). Annual billing available at $20/user/month (~$240/user/year).

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.notes: No public per-seat price. Sold only via annual contract through OpenAI sales; invoicing available as a payment option. Billing basis: annual (contract).

cons: ChatGPT's paid tiers do not publish hard usage caps: Plus ($20/month) usage is gated only by an unspecified 'Limits apply' note, and even the top $200/month Pro tier is capped as 'Unlimited subject to abuse guardrails' rather than a stated message/token quota, so a subscriber cannot know in advance exactly how much usage a given plan buys (per OpenAI's own official pricing/comparison page).

There is a steep price gap in the individual lineup: after Free ($0) and Plus ($20/month), the next real capability upgrade is Pro, which starts at $100/month and runs to $200/month -- a 5x to 10x jump from Plus with no $30-$60 mid-tier for individual users (the $8/month Go plan sits below Plus, not between Plus and Pro).

On OpenAI's own plan-comparison table, the Free, Go, and Plus consumer tiers are listed as 'Content is used to train our models,' with a separate 'Opt-out available' control -- meaning conversation data is used for model training by default unless the user proactively finds and enables the opt-out, rather than training use being opt-in.
